chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-'Askari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qushayri narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Harish Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon them all).
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And do not forget your share of the world" [28:77].
He said: Do not forget your health, your strength, your free time, your youth, and your vitality -- to seek the Hereafter through them.

key_terms.الآخرة: The Hereafter -- the eternal afterlife that should be the ultimate goal
key_terms.الدنيا: The world/worldly life -- the temporal realm whose blessings are means, not ends
key_terms.فراغ: Free time/leisure -- one of the five worldly blessings to be invested for the Hereafter
key_terms.نصيبك: Your share/portion -- reinterpreted as blessings like health and youth rather than material wealth

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali interpret the Quran verse "Do not forget your share of the world"?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) provides a profound reinterpretation of Quran 28:77 ("Do not forget your share of the world"). Rather than reading it as permission to enjoy worldly pleasures, he interprets "your share of the world" as the blessings of health, strength, leisure, youth, and energy -- all of which should be used to earn rewards for the Hereafter. This teaching was transmitted through the chain of Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the consistent Shia understanding of prioritizing spiritual investment over material indulgence.
